research_attempts.query_text: Richard D Walk; NARA OSS index context; CIA Reading Room exact-name domain check; Library of Congress exact-name collection check; exact-name and meaningful variants; OSS, rank, branch, identifier and assignment clues; employer and occupation 1940; obituary, institutional, newspaper, directory and archival searches; indexed Box 812; protected identifiers used only in private official-record comparison
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Unbridged namesakes, snippets, commercial people-finder pages, relatives, unsourced genealogy, postwar-only leads, and sources without an OSS, protected-identifier, rank, unit, or personnel-file bridge were rejected. Fred L. Walker Jr.'s compatible 36th Division lead was not assigned without a second corroborating identifier beyond name and rank. Gordon A Walker's material Army-name collision was rejected. Historical occupations were not converted into named employers.
research_attempts.research_notes: A reviewed protected-identifier Army bridge supports identity and a qualified architect category at Army entry; it supplies no named employer or OSS-transfer date. A postwar contractor-license namesake was not used as a wartime identity or employment bridge. Exact-name OSS, employer, occupation, obituary, institutional, newspaper, official-domain, and archival searches were checked as applicable. Grouped CIA Reading Room and Library of Congress discovery checks produced no additional publishable employer source for the cohort. The NARA index page was text-extracted, rendered, and visually checked; official Army bulk data, technical documentation, and code documentation were inspected locally. The code-787 page was also visually checked. No search-result snippet was used as sole final evidence, no paywall or access control was bypassed, and no authenticated NARA Catalog API call was made.
research_attempts.next_action: Review the indexed Box 812 personnel file for corroborating identifiers, the immediate pre-OSS affiliation, and the last civilian employer before wartime service.
